To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lowest rotor core eddy current losses are achieved with a distributed winding and double-layer rotor, and that a single-layer rotor is preferable for a concentrated winding.

the rotor eddy-current losses can be minimized by replacing the concentrated winding with a distributed one and by adding a second layer of permanent magnets to the rotor, which increases the magnet volume fraction and thus the magnet material losses.
the lowest total rotor core eddy- current losses in the machine are achieved using a distributed stator winding and a two-layer per-pole-rotor.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rotor core losses can be reduced significantly by using two magnet layers and a concentrated winding, and that the rotor core loss reduction is more important than the stator winding loss reduction.
the total machine-core eddy-current losses can be minimized using a combination of a two-layer rotor and a distributed stator winding.
the rotor core edy-current losses in IPM machines are a complex phenomenon that is influenced by a number of factors and that cannot be minimized by a single design approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rotor core edy-current losses in IPM machines are strongly dependent on the stator winding type and rotor magnet configuration.

the rotor core ed dy-current loss in IPM synchronous machines is a function of the rotor pole number, magnet layer thickness, and magnet material properties, whereas the stator core eddy-current loss is a function of stator winding type, number of slots per pole and per phase, and magnet material.

the total eddy-current loss in the machine core can be minimized using the combination of distributed stators and a double layer rotor, while minimizing only the rotor eddy-current loss favors the single-layer rotor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stator winding configuration and the rotor magnet layering are the two most important parameters that affect the eddy-current losses, and that they should be taken into consideration when designing IPM machines for high-efficiency applications.

the rotor core ed dy-current losses of IPMs can be significantly reduced using distributed windings in combination with a two-layer rotor. This is in stark contrast with the rotor eddy-current losses that occur in induction machines,

the rotor core eddycurrent losses of IPM synchronous machines are significantly affected by the stator winding configuration, and this should be considered when selecting the stator and rotor configurations.
